html:
The global economic landscape is increasingly defined by US-led trade and economic conflicts, with Canada announcing retaliatory tariffs against fresh US measures and President Trump declaring "economic warfare" on Iran, which Tehran condemns as a "declaration of war" on all nations.

North American Trade: A new trade war is brewing as Canada’s prime minister, Carney, reluctantly announced retaliatory tariffs against the US, accusing it of initiating the conflict. This follows the US imposing 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian products, which Canada will match "dollar for dollar" starting September 8. Carney now faces a crucial test to justify walking away from trade talks with the White House.

US-Iran Conflict: President Trump's declaration of "economic warfare" on Iran has been met with defiance from Tehran, which labels US sanctions a "declaration of war" on all nations and claims to have inflicted a strategic defeat on the US and Israel. Iran’s president, Masoud Pezeshkian, stated it is time to end the war from a "position of strength and dignity," while China rejects Trump’s push for further sanctions. Despite US claims that oil is flowing, traffic in the Strait of Hormuz remains significantly below pre-war levels, and Iran’s Ministry of Defense claims sanctions have spurred a doubling of defense equipment production.

Ukraine War Escalation: The conflict in Ukraine continues with deadly Russian strikes, including an attack on a shopping mall in Kryvyi Rih that killed 16 and injured 130, prompting Zelensky to condemn the "despicable" act. In response to fresh waves of Russian attacks, French President Emmanuel Macron announced Paris would deliver new interceptor missiles to Ukraine. Meanwhile, Ukrainian drone strikes targeted Russian refineries, depots, and an online retailer’s warehouse, killing at least 10 people and leading Putin to accuse Kyiv of opening a "Pandora's box" by striking economic targets. Russia has begun importing fuel due to shortages from these strikes, and German sappers are assisting Poland in building a defense system against Russia.

Middle East Tensions: Diplomatic pressure is mounting on Israel as France, Germany, the UK, and Italy, along with Arab and Muslim foreign ministers, condemned Israel’s ‘E1’ West Bank plan and settlement expansion. An open letter signed by 102 former French and and UK diplomats accused Israel of "ethnic cleansing" and urged their governments to ban trade and arms sales. In a major development, Turkey issued an arrest warrant for Israel’s Netanyahu, who retaliated by calling Turkey's president an "antisemitic dictator." Israel continued airstrikes and demolitions across southern Lebanon and carried out an incursion into Quneitra. The US, meanwhile, adopted a new classification, and Israel plans its offensive, tightening the noose around Hezbollah.

Global Economy & Society: The US debt has surpassed $40 trillion, raising concerns, while Australia has passed new laws requiring major tech platforms like Google and Meta to pay for Australian news content. A US federal judge struck down Trump's policy suspending immigrant visa processing for nationals of 75 countries, ruling it "contrary to law." On the technological front, a humanoid robot set a new 100m world record at the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, showcasing rapid advancements in robotics alongside a robot horse and rider at a Chinese conference. Meanwhile, the Democratic Republic of Congo received Ebola vaccines amid warnings that the current outbreak could surpass previous records.
